text.text_excerpt: I used to visit this place alot more when I worked closer to the Treme' area, but it seems nothing has changed. And that's in a good way. The owner is super sweet and helpful. Small little spot that always has a music selection playing that makes you want a copy to take home with you. Now on to the food. You know that cute little white lady with the saying from the Franks Red Hot commercial?!?! *Insert Catfish Reagan sauce there*. You'll want to put that shit on EVERYTHANG!!! Charbroiled oysters, fried fish, seafood pasta, Steak and potatoes all were amazing! There's also a signature drink.....the "Strong Ass Drink" yeah...the name nor drink disappoints. They also have cheap $5-$10 lunch ...

A GREAT little cafe. Tasty tasty local cuisine. Everyone seemed to know each other there...it was more like dinner at your cousin's house. Laid back, friendly. The food was great (I had the crispy chicken platter) and I will definitely try to make it in during the day for the lunch specials. Tiger himself was working on this Friday night so it was straight from the chef himself!! If you order the S.A.D (you'll just have to find out for yourself if you're over 21) be sure to have a DD!!

I've never been to the actual restaurant, but had the distinct pleasure and joy of sampling their fare at the Gumbo Festival in Louis Armstrong Park a few weeks ago. My boyfriend and I ate our way through that whole festival and both think Tigers was the best. The gumbo was hands down the best we sampled that day. We also tried Catfish Ragan which was phenomenal. It was delicious fried catfish on top of pasta in a creamy sauce. Delicious. I would recommend getting your hands on some Tigers, be it at their restaurant or at a festival-any way you can, if you're in NOLA.
